- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.8) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly.
- When sentiment is negative (≤0.2) or shows recent volatility, model often underestimates; adjust upward, especially if price is trending up.
- Model frequently overshoots after sharp spikes in sentiment or price; apply a 1–2 day lag correction to avoid overreaction.
- If true outcome shows strong mean reversion (e.g., price drops after peak), model tends to hold high; reduce forecast by 2–5% for next period.
- For 30-day horizon, model often fails to capture sentiment-driven momentum; weight sentiment history more heavily in later forecast days.
- If sentiment turns negative after a spike, model may not adjust quickly; add a downward bias of 1–3% for 2–3 days post-spike.
